obligation: G090 -- adaptive shortlist with verified fallback, and the protection the verify names
shortlist_reading: A cheap pass followed by exact rescoring of the top-k is only safe if the exact argmax is IN the cheap top-k. Recall@32 is the number that matters, because rescoring 32 rows costs 32*5120 = 163,840 elements against the head's 1.27e9 -- 0.013%, free.
rare_token_gap: THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH RARE-TOKEN SAFETY, which the verify explicitly requires. The capture produced only 42 distinct argmax tokens over 256 positions and G049 recorded vocabulary coverage at 0.128% of the vocab. Recall measured on that distribution says nothing about the 99.87% of tokens never observed. The per-row error stratification below is the only rare-token evidence available and it is a proxy, not a behavioural check.

cheap_pass_must_actually_be_cheap.why: A shortlist only pays if the cheap pass costs less than the exact one, and on this machine lower bits do NOT imply lower time: G072 measured flat q3 at 0.8521 ps/element, SLOWER than q4's 0.8425. A q2 cheap pass would very likely cost more than the exact q4 pass it replaces, so the recall numbers for flat codecs above do not translate into a saving.
cheap_pass_must_actually_be_cheap.verdict: binary planes k1 runs the head in 0.770 ms against q4's 1.071, saving 0.301 ms, and its top-8 shortlist recovers the exact argmax on 100.0% of tested positions. Exact rescoring of 8 rows is 40,960 elements against 1.27e9 -- 0.003%, free.

special_token_risk: Special tokens (ids >= 248000) carry systematically HIGHER row error than ordinary ones at every precision that matters: 1.37x at flat q3, 1.63x at flat q4, and 2.31x at planes k1. This is exactly the behaviour the verify singles out for protection, and it is a real signal rather than noise -- the special block is represented worse than the vocabulary it sits beside.
